title: Supreme Court: North Carolina v. Covington
summary: The District Court’s order is affirmed insofar as it provided a court-drawn remedy for Senate Districts 21 and 28 and House Districts 21 and 57 and reversed as to the court’s actions concerning the legislature’s redrawing of House districts in Wake and Mecklenburg Counties. (No. 17-1364, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 585 U.S. 969).

title: Supreme Court: Sexton v. Beaudreaux
summary: The Ninth Circuit erred in reversing a denial of federal habeas relief on the ground that the state court had unreasonably rejected respondent’s ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claim. (No. 17-1106, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 585 U.S. 961).

title: Supreme Court: Sause v. Bauer
summary: The Tenth Circuit erred in holding that police officers were entitled to qualified immunity without considering the ground on which the officers were present in petitioner’s home and the nature of any legitimate law enforcement interests that might have justified their order that petitioner stop praying at the specific time in question. (No. 17-742, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 585 U.S. 957).

title: Supreme Court: Janus v. State, County, and Municipal Employees
summary: The State of Illinois’ extraction of agency fees from nonconsenting public-sector employees violates the First Amendment; Abood v. Detroit Bd. of Ed., 431 U. S. 209, which concluded otherwise, is overruled. (No. 16-1466, opinion by Justice Alito; 585 U.S. 878).

title: Supreme Court: Florida v. Georgia
summary: Florida has made a legally sufficient showing as to the possibility of fashioning an effective remedial decree equitably apportioning the water from an interstate river basin. (No. 142, Orig., opinion by Justice Breyer; 585 U.S.803).

title: Supreme Court: National Institute of Family and Life Advocates v. Becerra
summary: Petitioners are likely to succeed on their claim that the California Reproductive Freedom, Accountability, Comprehensive Care, and Transparency Act (FACT Act) violates the First Amendment. (No. 16-1140, opinion by Justice Thomas; 585 U.S. 755).

title: Supreme Court: Trump v. Hawaii
summary: The President has lawfully exercised the broad discretion granted to him under 8 U. S. C. §1182(f) to suspend the entry of aliens into the United States; respondents have not demonstrated a likelihood of success on the merits of their claim that Presidential Proclamation No. 9645 violates the Establishment Clause. (No. 17-965, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 585 U.S. 667).

title: Supreme Court: Abbott v. Perez
summary: The District Court disregarded the presumption of legislative good faith and improperly reversed the burden of proof when it required the State to show a lack of discriminatory intent in adopting new districting plans; one of the challenged State House districts is an impermissible racial gerrymander. (No. 17-586, opinion by Justice Alito; 585 U.S. 579).

title: Supreme Court: Ohio v. American Express Co.
summary: American Express’ antisteering provisions in its merchant contracts—which prohibit merchants from avoiding fees by discouraging customers’ American Express card use at the point of sale—do not violate federal antitrust law. (No. 16-1454, opinion by Justice Thomas; 585 U.S. 529).

title: Supreme Court: Cox v. United States
summary: Certiorari dismissed as improvidently granted. (No. 16-1017, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 585 U.S. 528).

title: Supreme Court: Dalmazzi v. United States
summary: Certiorari dismissed as improvidently granted. (No. 16-961, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 585 U.S. 527).

title: Supreme Court: Currier v. Virginia
summary: Because Currier consented to a severance of the multiple charges against him, his second trial and resulting conviction, following an acquittal at his first trial, did not violate the Double Jeopardy Clause. (No. 16-1348, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 585 U.S. 493).

title: Supreme Court: Ortiz v. United States
summary: Military Judge Mitchell’s simultaneous service on an Air Force appeals court and the Court of Military Commission Review violated neither 10 U. S. C. §973(b)(2)(A) nor the Appointments Clause. (No. 16-1423, opinion by Justice Kagan; 585 U.S. 427).

title: Supreme Court: WesternGeco LLC v. ION Geophysical Corp.
summary: The focus of the Patent Act’s general damages provision, 35 U. S. C. §284, in a case involving infringement under §271(f)(2) is on the act of exporting components from the United States; therefore, WesternGeco’s award for lost profits was a permissible domestic application of §284, not an extraterritorial one. (No. 16-1011, opinion by Justice Thomas; 585 U.S. 407).

title: Supreme Court: Carpenter v. United States
summary: The Government’s acquisition of Carpenter’s cell-site records from his wireless carriers was a Fourth Amendment search; and the Government did not obtain a warrant supported by probable cause before acquiring those records. (No. 16-402, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 585 U.S. 296).

title: Supreme Court: Wisconsin Central Ltd. v. United States
summary: Employee stock options are not taxable “compensation” under the Railroad Retirement Tax Act of 1937. (No. 17-530, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 585 U.S. 274).

title: Supreme Court: Lucia v. SEC
summary: Securities and Exchange Commission administrative law judges are “Officers of the United States,” subject to the Appointments Clause. (No. 17-130, opinion by Justice Kagan; 585 U.S. 237).

title: Supreme Court: Pereira v. Sessions
summary: A putative notice sent to a nonpermanent resident to appear at a removal proceeding that fails to designate a specific time or place for that proceeding does not end the continuous residence period calculation necessary for possible cancellation of the individual’s removal. (No. 17-459, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 585 U.S. 198).

title: Supreme Court: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc.
summary: Quill Corp. v. North Dakota, 504 U. S. 298, and National Bellas Hess, Inc. v. Department of Revenue of Ill., 386 U. S. 753—which held that a State cannot require an out-of-state seller with no physical presence in the State to collect and remit sales taxes on goods the seller ships to consumers in the State—are overruled. (No. 17-494, opinion by Justice Kennedy; 585 U.S. 162).

title: Supreme Court: Benisek v. Lamone
summary: Because the balance of equities and the public interest tilt against the preliminary injunction motion of plaintiffs claiming that a Maryland congressional district was gerrymandered to retaliate against them for their political views, the District Court did not abuse its discretion in denying the motion. (No. 17-333, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 585 U.S. 155).

title: Supreme Court: Rosales-Mireles v. United States
summary: A miscalculation of a Federal Guidelines sentencing range that has been determined to be plain and to affect a defendant’s substantial rights calls for a court of appeals to exercise its discretion under Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 52(b) to vacate the defendant’s sentence in the ordinary case. (No. 16-9493, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 585 U.S. 129).

title: Supreme Court: Chavez-Meza v. United States
summary: Because the record in this case demonstrates that the judge had a reasoned basis for his decision, the judge’s explanation for reducing, under 18 U. S. C. §3582(c)(2), petitioner’s sentence to the middle rather than the bottom of the amended Federal Guidelines range was adequate. (No. 17-5639, opinion by Justice Breyer; 585 U.S. 109).

title: Supreme Court: Lozman v. Riviera Beach
summary: The existence of probable cause for Lozman’s arrest for disrupting a city council meeting does not bar his First Amendment retaliatory arrest claim under the circumstances of this case. (No. 17-21, opinion by Justice Kennedy; 585 U.S. 87).

title: Supreme Court: Gill v. Whitford
summary: Plaintiffs—Wisconsin Democratic voters who rested their claim of unconstitutional partisan gerrymandering on statewide injury—have failed to demonstrate Article III standing. (No. 16-1161, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 585 U.S. 48).

title: Supreme Court: Animal Science Products, Inc. v. Hebei Welcome Pharmaceutical Co.
summary: A federal court determining foreign law under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 44.1 should accord respectful consideration to a foreign government’s submission, but the court is not bound to accord conclusive effect to the foreign government’s statements. (No. 16-1220, opinion by Justice Ginsburg; 585 U.S. 33).

title: Supreme Court: Minnesota Voters Alliance v. Mansky
summary: Minnesota’s ban on political apparel at polling places violates the First Amendment’s Free Speech Clause. (No. 16-1435, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 585 U.S. 1).

title: Supreme Court: Washington v. United States
summary: Judgment affirmed by an equally divided Court. (No. 17-269, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 584 U.S. 837).

title: Supreme Court: Sveen v. Melin
summary: The retroactive application of Minnesota’s revocation-on-divorce statute—which automatically nullifies an ex-spouse’s beneficiary designation on a life-insurance policy or other will substitute—does not violate the Contracts Clause. (No. 16-1432, opinion by Justice Kagan; 584 U.S. 811).

title: Supreme Court: Husted v. A. Philip Randolph Institute
summary: The process that Ohio uses to remove voters on change-of-residence grounds does not violate the National Voter Registration Act. (No. 16-980, opinion by Justice Alito; 584 U.S. 756).

title: Supreme Court: China Agritech, Inc. v. Resh
summary: Upon denial of class certification, a putative class member may not, in lieu of promptly joining an existing suit or promptly filing an individual action, commence a class action anew beyond the time allowed by the applicable statute of limitations. (No. 17-432, opinion by Justice Ginsburg; 584 U.S. 732).

title: Supreme Court: Azar v. Garza
summary: The D. C. Circuit’s judgment is vacated, and the case is remanded with instructions to dismiss the individual claim for injunctive relief as moot. (No. 17-654, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 584 U.S. 726).

title: Supreme Court: Lamar, Archer & Cofrin, LLP v. Appling
summary: Single-asset statements qualify as “statement[s] respecting the debtor’s . . . financial condition” for purposes of Bankruptcy Code §523(a)(2)’s exceptions to discharge; where, as here, a single-asset statement is not in writing, the associated debt may be discharged. (No. 16-1215, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 584 U.S. 709).

title: Supreme Court: Koons v. United States
summary: Petitioners do not qualify for sentence reductions under 18 U. S. C. §3582(c)(2) because their sentences were not “based on” their lowered Federal Sentencing Guidelines ranges but, instead, were “based on” their mandatory minimums and their substantial assistance to the Government. (No. 17-5716, opinion by Justice Alito; 584 U.S. 700).

title: Supreme Court: Hughes v. United States
summary: A Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 11(c)(1)(C) plea agreement is “based on” the defendant’s Federal Sentencing Guidelines range so long as that range was part of the framework the district court relied on in imposing the sentence or accepting the agreement; thus, Hughes may seek a sentencing reduction under 18 U. S. C. §3582(c)(2). (No. 17-155, opinion by Justice Kennedy; 584 U.S. 675).

title: Supreme Court: Masterpiece Cakeshop, Ltd. v. Colorado Civil Rights Comm’n
summary: The Colorado Civil Rights Commission’s actions in assessing a cakeshop owner’s reasons for declining to make a cake for a same-sex couple’s wedding celebration violated the Free Exercise Clause. (No. 16-111, opinion by Justice Kennedy; 584 U.S. 617).
